title: Reformulation-Contrastive Learning for Mixed Integer Programs
abstract: Mixed-integer linear programs (MILP) model many real-world decision problems, motivating machine-learning methods that exploit recurring structure to accelerate MILP solving. MILPs can admit many equivalent formulations: integrality-preserving changes of variables and the addition of redundant constraints can alter their formulations while preserving the optimization problem. We leverage these reformulations as a source of self-supervision for learning general-purpose representations of MILP variables and constraints. We characterize the affine reformulations that are valid for every input instance, and distinguish re-descriptions, which leave variables unchanged, from substitutions, which transform them predictably. Building on equivariant self-supervised learning, we introduce ReMILP (reformulation-contrastive MILP representation learning), which jointly trains a graph neural network and a hypernetwork to predict how variable embeddings transform under changes of variables. Without solver-derived labels, ReMILP learns representations that exhibit the intended invariance and equivariance on unseen problem classes. Across binary solution, constraint activity and integrality gap prediction, these representations carry task-relevant information when frozen and provide a useful initialization for fine-tuning.

title: Refined sample complexities from the tomographic rate function
abstract: Protocols for quantum state tomography can be characterized either by their sample complexity or by the tomographic rate function that governs the large deviation behaviour of error estimates. We establish a framework for the analysis of covariant protocols which allows us to compare these measures. First, we derive the rate functions for several protocols, including random purification-based protocols and the sample-optimal protocol of Haah et al. These rate functions are expressed in terms of a new family of divergences which includes the reverse sandwiched Rényi divergence and Keyl's annealed quantum relative entropy as special cases. We show that these rate functions obey a strict ordering, even though the sample complexity of each protocol is order optimal. We consider a different version of sample complexity based on Wasserstein distance rather than trace distance, and show that the ordering of the rate functions implies analogous strict inequalities for the Wasserstein-type sample complexity. Thus the tomographic rate function is a more fine-grained indicator of the performance of a tomography protocol than the usual sample complexity.

title: Perfect non-local quantum computation is impossible
abstract: Non-local quantum computation (NLQC) asks two parties to apply a joint operation to their quantum inputs using an entangled resource state and one round of simultaneous quantum communication. NLQC has applications across quantum information, including attacks on quantum position verification, communication complexity, and quantum gravity. Every bipartite unitary has an approximate NLQC protocol with finite entanglement, and exact protocols are known for several structured families. However, it has remained open whether every fixed unitary admits an exact protocol with finite-dimensional resources. We show that, even for two qubits, Haar-almost every unitary does not admit such a protocol, even when the resource state and local operations are tailored to the target. The proof first shows that smooth deformations of an exact protocol can only change its target by local unitaries. For a fixed architecture, semialgebraic geometry limits the exact protocols to finitely many connected families, so each architecture reaches only finitely many local-unitary orbits. Taking the union over all architectures, the exactly implementable unitaries form countably many local-unitary orbits. We also show that some natural targets do not admit a protocol: the controlled phase $\mathrm{diag}(1,1,1,e^{iθ})$ has no exact protocol with finite-dimensional resources whenever $e^{iθ}$ is transcendental, for instance for $θ= 1$. Our results also apply to localizable quantum measurements, whose outcome is obtained from local measurements on inputs and a shared entangled resource state without communication. A rank-one projective measurement in a Haar-random basis is almost surely not localizable with a finite-dimensional resource state and finitely many local outcomes.

title: Hybrid Methods for Robust Tabular Data Imputation
abstract: Missing data are a fundamental challenge in statistical analysis and machine learning, as the choice of imputation method substantially impacts downstream inference. In this work, we propose two hybrid imputation methods called NuclearForest and SoftForest, which combine nuclear-norm-based low-rank initialization using Singular Value Thresholding (SVT) and SoftImpute, respectively, with a non-iterative Random Forest refinement. For the SVT-based component, we further introduce an adaptive step-size rule, prove adaptive step-size bounds, and establish convergence for the corresponding zero-initialized iteration. The low-rank initialization provides a structured warm start that captures the global covariance patterns in the data, while the subsequent Random Forest step recovers residual nonlinear signals encoding local dependencies. We conduct an extensive benchmark on diverse datasets from different application domains, comparing the proposed methods with seven established imputation methods under the Missing Completely at Random (MCAR), Missing at Random (MAR), and Missing Not at Random (MNAR) mechanisms across varying missingness rates. Our results demonstrate that NuclearForest and SoftForest match or exceed the imputation fidelity of state-of-the-art iterative methods such as MissForest, while significantly reducing computational cost. In particular, they achieve speedups of approximately 5.81 times and 9.52 times over MissForest by replacing iterative cycles with a single refinement step. evidence.title: Hybrid Methods for Robust Tabular Data Imputation
evidence.abstract: Missing data are a fundamental challenge in statistical analysis and machine learning, as the choice of imputation method substantially impacts downstream inference. In this work, we propose two hybrid imputation methods called NuclearForest and SoftForest, which combine nuclear-norm-based low-rank initialization using Singular Value Thresholding (SVT) and SoftImpute, respectively, with a non-iterative Random Forest refinement. For the SVT-based component, we further introduce an adaptive step-size rule, prove adaptive step-size bounds, and establish convergence for the corresponding zero-initialized iteration. The low-rank initialization provides a structured warm start that captures the global covariance patterns in the data, while the subsequent Random Forest step recovers residual nonlinear signals encoding local dependencies. We conduct an extensive benchmark on diverse datasets from different application domains, comparing the proposed methods with seven established imputation methods under the Missing Completely at Random (MCAR), Missing at Random (MAR), and Missing Not at Random (MNAR) mechanisms across varying missingness rates. Our results demonstrate that NuclearForest and SoftForest match or exceed the imputation fidelity of state-of-the-art iterative methods such as MissForest, while significantly reducing computational cost. In particular, they achieve speedups of approximately 5.81 times and 9.52 times over MissForest by replacing iterative cycles with a single refinement step. Our approach effectively exploits the low-rank structure of real-world tabular data and accommodates mixed-type variables, providing an efficient and robust solution for data imputation in bioinformatics, economics, and beyond.

title: Beyond Simulation: Retain-and-Repair Neural Operators for Real-World Adaptation
abstract: Neural operators increasingly benefit from pretraining on numerical simulations, yet adapting them for real-world prediction remains challenging. We introduce the Retain-and-Repair Neural Operator (R$^2$NO), a framework for adapting simulation-pretrained operators to real-world data while retaining useful pretrained structure. The pretrained operator is first finetuned on real data and then frozen to provide a source prediction, and a shared repair module learns a sequence of refinements from the same observations. Using orthogonal Fourier projections, a spectral ensemble fits a small ridge regression within each cell of the Fourier domain and combines the refinements by weights fitted on a held-out split of the real data. The cells are defined jointly by radial ranges, angular sectors, and measured channels, allowing refinement depth to vary with frequency magnitude, with orientation, and across channels. Including the source prediction as a candidate makes retention available in every cell, and independently trained repair modules enter the same combination as additional candidates. On all RealPDEBench systems and six backbones, R$^2$NO consistently outperforms full finetuning and iterative refinement. The framework treats adaptation depth as a cell-specific choice learned from real data.

title: Aligning Thoughts with Answers: Probability Rewards to Tame Thinking Drift
abstract: This paper studies \textbf{thinking--answer consistency} in vision-language models. We focus on Visual Intention Grounding, where a model infers a target object based on a human intention query and predicts a bounding box. We reveal that previous IoU-based reinforcement learning (RL) frameworks suffer from ``thinking drift'', where the model produces a correct bounding box, despite having an incorrect reasoning process pointing to a different target object. Thus, we propose \textbf{Rita} (\textit{ReInforcing Thinking--Answer consistency}) as a novel RL paradigm to tame the drift. Specifically, Rita introduces two reasoning-label-free RL rewards, constructed from the conditional probability of reference answers: a \textbf{thinking reward} and a \textbf{consistency reward}. It also adopts a difficulty-aware \textbf{data filtering} strategy that selects informative easy-to-medium samples for RL using rollout error rate and reward variance. Extensive experiments on EgoIntention and the new RefEgo-Int benchmarks show that Rita performs consistently superior to the supervised finetuning approaches and vanilla RL-finetuned frameworks.

title: Evaluating The Impact Of Spectral Band Integration On 3D-CNN Performance For Mineral Identification
abstract: Remote sensing plays a vital role in mineral exploration by offering cost-effective, large-scale, and non-invasive mapping solutions. However, many advanced mineral classification approaches rely heavily on hyperspectral data, which are costly, computationally demanding, and often lack global availability. This study evaluates the performance of extended spectral input combinations using ASTER multispectral imagery for mineral classification in skarn-type iron deposits of the Western Tianshan Mountains, China. While the earlier study demonstrated the potential of integrating selected band ratio (BR) images and principal component (PC) bands with ASTER data, the present research expands this by systematically assessing six additional configurations, including: (1) all 9 bands, (2) all 15 BR images, (3) a combined input of all PCs and BRs, (4) ASTER original bands with all PCs, (5) ASTER bands with all BRs, and (6) ASTER bands combined with both all PCs and all BRs. A 3D Convolutional Neural Network (3D-CNN) model was used to evaluate how spectral feature selection impacts mineral classification accuracy and model behavior. The results revealed significant variability in performance across configurations. Using all PCs alone achieved an overall accuracy (OA) of 89.31%, outperforming all BRs (OA = 84.73%), while the combined use of all PCs and BRs yielded the lowest accuracy (OA = 79.39%), likely due to spectral redundancy. In contrast, the best classification results were obtained using a targeted integration of ASTER bands, selected PCs, and selected BRs, achieving an OA of 98.64% and Kappa coefficient of 98.27%. The study also identified persistent misclassification challenges, with over 50% of skarn samples misidentified as wall rocks or intrusions and approximately 35% of intrusions misclassified as skarn or wall rock in certain setups. These issues were mitigated through optimized spectral integration, which enhanced class separability without the need for hyperspectral inputs. The findings demonstrate that a systematically optimized, sensor-flexible spectral strategy using ASTER data can deliver high classification performance while reducing the complexity, cost, and processing burden associated with hyperspectral approaches.

title: Intelligent Natural Language Processing Frameworks for Real-Time Customer Feedback Analysis in Digital Service Ecosystems
abstract: The proliferation of digital service ecosystems has generated unprecedented volumes of unstructured customer feedback across platforms, creating both opportunities and challenges for organizations seeking to understand and respond to user experiences in real time. This research article presents a comprehensive investigation into intelligent Natural Language Processing (NLP) frameworks designed for real-time customer feedback analysis within digital service environments. Drawing upon recent advances in transformer-based architectures, Large Language Models (LLMs), and streaming data processing, the study proposes an integrated architectural framework that addresses critical limitations in existing approaches, including disjointed sentiment extraction, lack of contextual strategic weighting, and latency in feedback processing. The proposed framework combines multi-tier sentiment classification, intent detection, anomaly identification, and automated decision routing to transform passive customer data into actionable business intelligence. Through analysis of benchmark datasets and platform-specific implementations, the research demonstrates significant improvements in processing speed, classification accuracy, and insight generation. Findings indicate that intelligent NLP frameworks can reduce feedback resolution times, improve personalization accuracy, and explain substantial variation in satisfaction outcomes. The study contributes both theoretical understanding of NLP application in customer experience management and practical guidance for implementing real-time feedback architectures in digital service ecosystems.

title: Agastya AGI v01 Native Brain Evidence Release R1
abstract: Agastya AGI v01 is a sovereign, from-scratch native foundation-model program developed in India by Rabbit Industries Pvt Ltd under the Bramha Medha Native INDIA family. Agastya Native Brain Evidence Release R1 publishes the cryptographically anchored provenance of the canonical Agastya Native Brain lineage and is intended to make the project externally citable, reproducible at the evidence layer, and suitable for independent technical verification. The canonical development lineage is: Agastya corpus → Agastya tokenizer → Agastya architecture → RANDOM INITIALIZATION → Agastya pretraining → Agastya post-training → Agastya Native Brain The evidence package records and publishes: Fresh random initialization at step 0 — PASS Teacher-weight ancestry — ZERO Third-party weight ancestry — FALSE Third-party tokenizer artifact import — FALSE Unique parameter count — 1,264,715,776 Architecture class — dense native model Canonical context length — 4,096 tokens Native tokenizer vocabulary — 98,320 entries Tokenizer, architecture, initialization and checkpoint provenance — SHA-256 anchored Checkpoint validation — PASS Clean-P0 zero-third-party acceptance — PASS The release includes a technical evidence report, machine-readable weight-lineage and tokenizer-provenance manifests, checkpoint-validation evidence, Clean-P0 acceptance evidence, source-artifact hashes, package checksums, citation metadata, and an independent-verification protocol. The canonical Agastya Native Brain does not inherit, merge, distill, or initialize from third-party model weights. Reference models may be used separately for evaluation and comparative research, but they are not part of the canonical Agastya weight ancestry. This public evidence release intentionally does not redistribute proprietary raw model weights, the raw training corpus, the complete tokenizer vocabulary/merges artifact, private architecture source code, or proprietary training source code. These artifacts are retained by Rabbit Industries and can be made available under controlled conditions to qualified independent evaluators for provenance verification. Independent third-party verification of the complete lineage is the next external validation gate. Same-suite public benchmark qualification against contemporary frontier systems will follow using frozen model versions, evaluation harnesses, prompts, scoring procedures, tool permissions, and reproducible environments. No independently verified global performance rank is claimed in this R1 release. Rabbit Industries is pursuing independent verification, DOI-backed preservation, public model documentation, frozen same-suite benchmark evaluation, and external leaderboard acceptance so that future capability claims are supported by directly comparable evidence. India positioning: Agastya is developed in India by Rabbit Industries Pvt Ltd as a from-scratch sovereign native foundation-model program with publicly released cryptographic provenance evidence. Rabbit Industries is pursuing independent prior-art and technical verification for a narrower India-first distinction based on independently verified native lineage, zero third-party weight ancestry, and independently verified tokenizer provenance. Global objective: Agastya is designed and being evaluated for global frontier competitiveness while maintaining sovereign model provenance and native development principles. title: The Universal Law of Recursive Meta-Stochastic Alignment (RMA)
abstract: This paper introduces and formalizes the Law of Recursive Meta-Stochastic Alignment (\Omega_{RMA}), a universal cybernetic and systemic principle governing all hierarchical systems under zero-information conditions. We demonstrate that when a meta-level (Order-2) node attempts to evaluate a primary-level (Order-1) stochastic event without receiving inter-order information transfer (I(X;Y)=0), the meta-node recursively clones the primary stochastic process. This paper presents a profound philosophical grounding based on the subjective "guessing paradox," followed by an exhaustive objective mathematical formalization, parameterization, and structural topology. Furthermore, it analyzes ten real-world cross-domain case studies, provides Python simulation proofs, and maps the future horizons of this systemic law.

title: The Burden-Relative Closure: A Complete Route Through Determination, Preservation, Distinction, Articulation, Repair, and Transition
abstract: The Burden-Relative Closure consolidates a sequence of Tier-2 results in Structura Reditus into one exact route through determination, preservation, distinction, heterogeneous articulation, evidential repair, and burden transition. The paper begins from an admitted domain \(X\), a retained representation family \(\mathcal A=\{E_1,\ldots,E_m\}\), and a nonempty finite family of independently warranted exact burdens \(\mathcal B=\{B_1,\ldots,B_r\}\). Writing \(E_{\mathcal A}\) for the joint representation and \(F_{\mathcal B}\) for the joint burden signature, exact burden-relative sufficiency is characterized by the equality-fiber condition \ker E_{\mathcal A}\subseteq\ker F_{\mathcal B}, equivalently by the absence of a pair that is merged by the retained representation while still distinguished by the active burden. The unresolved set \mathcal U_{\mathcal B}(E_{\mathcal A}) = \mathcal C_{E_{\mathcal A}}\cap\mathcal D_{\mathcal B} therefore localizes exact insufficiency. Repair requires genuinely separating information; deterministic restatement of an unchanged insufficient record cannot repair the burden. These fixed-burden results unify determination, burden-relative preservation, decisive collision, joint sufficiency, strict complementarity, and evidential deepening under one exact relation. The_Burden_Relative_Closure_v1.… The paper then introduces burden transition as a second independent axis. Same-domain predecessor and successor burdens are classified by equality-kernel inclusion, while predecessor-output transfer is kept distinct from fresh determination by retained evidence. This yields an exhaustive successor route: direct transfer when the predecessor output determines the successor; fresh determination when transfer fails but retained evidence remains sufficient; and evidential repair when the retained evidence also fails. The paper further establishes a safe-direction monotonicity result and an exact route-completeness theorem for the declared Tier-2 domain. The_Burden_Relative_Closure_v1.… The resulting closure is explicitly burden-relative and formal. It does not establish empirical coverage, normative authority, support, identity, provenance, historical continuity, canonical return, seam closure, weld, ledger reconciliation, or final stance. Those stronger conclusions remain governed by their own evidence, authority, transport, contract, and Tier-0 conditions.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering on the Grain-Boundary Diffusion Literature of NdFeB Permanent Magnets: A Comparison of Commercial and Local Large Language Models
abstract: The grain-boundary diffusion process (GBDP) is the leading route to high coercivity in NdFeB permanent magnets with reduced heavy-rare-earth (HRE) content, and its rapidly growing literature is increasingly difficult to synthesize. We built a retrieval-augmented-generation (RAG) system over a corpus of 311 GBDP papers that uses lightweight, CPU-only sentence embeddings, section-aware chunking, and source-cited answer generation, and used it to com pare three large language models: the commercial GPT-4o and Gemini 3.5 Flash, and the locally served open-weight Llama 3.2. To separate the language model from the retriever, we adopted a controlled design in which retrieval was held constant so that all three models received an identical evidence set for each question, and answers were assessed qualitatively for faithfulness to the retrieved passages and for citation correctness. Across three representative questions (the advantage of GBDP, its diffusion sources and the role of HRE), the models’ factual grounding was comparable once the retrieved context was informative; removing duplicate documents from the index improved the retrieval of answer-bearing passages and reduced unsupported additions in the evaluated cases. The principal difference was citation reliability: both commercial models attributed every claim correctly, whereas the local model extracted correct content but omitted or misapplied source citations. Faithfulness thus emerged as a property of the retrieval stage as much as of the model. We conclude that RAG is a practical aid for consolidating dispersed GBDP knowledge, and that a local open-weight model is a viable privacy-preserving option provided its attribution is verified.

title: Development of a Low-Cost Automated Papanicolaou Slide Stainer with Preliminary Image-Based Cellular Localization
abstract: This study developed and evaluated a low-cost automated Papanicolaou slide stainer integrated with a preliminary image-processing module for localizing suspicious cellular regions. The prototype used a Raspberry Pi 4 to control three-axis stepper motors, a servo-driven slide-rack gripper, and a 5-inch touchscreen. Its aluminum-profile structure accommodated nine reagent jars and up to ten slides per cycle, although two slides per cycle were used during prototype testing. In ten experimental cycles, touchscreen start, stop, and position-selection commands achieved 100% success, while the automatic staining sequence achieved 90%. The X-axis operated successfully in all trials, whereas the Y- and Z-axes each achieved 90% success. The mean staining time was 67.04 min per cycle. The prototype’s staining quality received an overall mean score of 4.38 from expert evaluators. The image-processing workflow employed contrast enhancement, adaptive thresholding, watershed segmentation, and morphological feature extraction. title: LeanSide: A Formally Verified Co-Reasoning System for Natural-language Proofs
abstract: Large language models are increasingly used as collaborators on deductive-reasoning tasks, but their outputs can hallucinate or pull users away from intended reasoning. Formal proof assistants provide machine-checked verification, but have a steep learning curve and require more granular reasoning than human written proofs. We explore an interface that combines these strengths, allowing users to write and revise free-form natural-language proofs while a verified backend checks their reasoning and returns feedback at the user's granularity. We study this interface in the context of undergraduate mathematics education by developing LeanSide, a formally verified co-reasoning system, which auto-formalizes student reasoning into Lean and informalizes verifier output into understandable feedback. We conducted user studies through classroom deployment and analyzed which system properties helped students make progress and which caused them to get stuck. We use these findings to derive design implications for using a formally verified backend in human-AI co-reasoning systems.

title: Optimal two-mode bosonic loss codes from finite group symmetry
abstract: Photon loss is a dominant noise process in bosonic quantum hardware, including superconducting cavities. Fixed-total-photon-number qubit encodings in two bosonic modes retain the loss-detection advantage of dual-rail qubits while supporting photon loss correction. Optimizing entanglement fidelity in this setting for $4\leq n\leq25$ over arbitrary encoders and decoders reveals finite-group structure in every best-found code: 11 correspond to two-dimensional irreducible representations and 11 to reducible ones. Motivated by this emergence, we derive the necessary-and-sufficient Knill-Laflamme conditions for arbitrary finite-group-invariant codes, reducing their construction to equations on representation multiplicity spaces. For every finite subgroup of $SU(2)$ and every tensor rank, we explicitly construct the minimum number of operators required to impose all corresponding loss-correction constraints. These results produce analytic counterparts to most numerical codes and predict constructions missed by the initial search. Exact MacWilliams-Farkas certificates show that our codes achieve the maximum possible loss distance in 21 of the 22 sectors, and we prove that the resulting distance bound is monotone in total photon number. Beyond the scan, we identify a binary-polyhedral sequence with photon number $n_d=\lceil(3d^2+1)/4\rceil$ and construct each corresponding code through distance $d=10$. To our knowledge, the constructed $(n,d)=(28,6),(49,8),(76,10)$ codes give the smallest reported $n$ for their respective distances; all members through $d=9$ attain the fixed-$n$ LP distance bound. Together, these constructions, certificates, and a symmetry-reduced constraint count provide evidence for an infinite code family conjectured to attain every distance at the minimum photon number.

title: Multi-agent Auditory Scene Analysis: Improved Localization Speed and Robustness by Multi-beamformed Speech Quality Feedback
abstract: A real-time auditory scene analyzer (ASA) aims to carry out the tasks of locating, separating and classifying the sound sources present in a given acoustic environment. Recently, an effort has been made into modelling an ASA as a multi-agent system, with each one of its agents performing one of the aforementioned tasks and communicating their results to the rest of their peer agents. These communication routes are used as feedback loops to fix local errors at a global level, providing robustness while reducing local complexity. An example of the benefits of this approach is the optimization of speech quality by correcting in real-time the estimated location of the speech source of interest. However, their optimization speed has been shown to be considerably slow. One possible reason is that it solely relies on a series of single quality estimations (provided by a reference-free quality estimator model) that vary considerably from one window to the next, which results in a difficult search space to optimize. In this work, a new optimization mechanism is proposed that instead relies on a series of sets of quality estimations over a range of locations, providing a clearer view of the search space, simplifying its optimization. The proposed ASA now has a considerably smaller optimization time, is more accurate, and is more stable when being evaluated in real-life acoustic scenarios to correct higher levels of localization errors, all while being less complex than previous efforts. The only trade-off is that there is an increase in the response time of the quality estimation agent, but the complete ASA is still able to run in real-time. The performance shown in this work again shows the benefits of modelling an ASA as a multi-agent system.

title: RIQE: a NIQE-style reference model for Computed Tomography
abstract: The Natural Image Quality Evaluator (NIQE) scores an image by its statistical distance from a model fitted on pristine images, and its distributed model is fitted on photographs. We release the Radiology Image Quality Evaluator (RIQE), a NIQE-style model fitted on 3,792 full-dose slices from 158 patients of the public LDCT-and-Projection-data collection, with a declared intensity mapping, a manifest of every slice and a script that reproduces the fit. On 40 held-out patients, RIQE ranks reduced-dose reconstructions, simulated by projection-domain noise insertion, worse than the full-dose reconstruction of the same slice in 240 of 240 chest and 230 of 240 abdominal pairs, and ranks images with 20% more noise worse than their source in 97.5-100% of cases. Its preferences among filtered images, however, do not follow lesion signal. With a 4 mm, +10 HU lesion inserted in noisy abdominal slices, RIQE prefers bilateral filtering to the unfiltered image in every image up to a 32 HU residual, at which 29% of the lesion's matched-filter signal remains and its detectability index falls from 0.51 to 0.33; it never prefers Gaussian smoothing, which at the same 32 HU residual leaves 70% of the signal and a detectability index of 0.48. Fitted on photographs with the parameters published for NIQE, the same code ranks every simulated reduced-dose abdominal image better than its full-dose counterpart. RIQE is suited to ranking a degraded image against its source; under the conditions tested it should not be the sole criterion for selecting, comparing or tuning denoisers.

title: Beyond Model Ranking: Regime Diagnosis for Distributional-Statistical Misspecification in Industrial Time-Series Forecasting
abstract: Time-series forecasting models achieve strong benchmark performance but exhibit severe systematic bias in industrial deployments. This train--deploy gap is conventionally attributed to temporal-structural errors or distribution shifts. We characterize a complementary source that these explanations overlook: canonical losses embed fixed statistical priors, while industrial demand mixes benign and pathological regimes---zero-inflation, skewness, high variability---in which these priors are systematically violated. The induced bias persists even under perfect temporal modeling, remains in a distributional-shape component that normalization cannot remove, and creates an aggregation trade-off invisible to aggregate metrics. We turn these observations into an evaluation toolkit centered on the Regime-wise Relative Bias Vector (RBV): a metric-agnostic, regime-decomposed diagnostic that audits how pooled training allocates systematic mismatch across pathological subpopulations. A controlled attribution analysis decomposes RBV into a model-independent intrinsic floor, set by each loss's estimand, and an excess component attributable to training, tracing observed bias to the loss rather than the model. A large-scale study---13 loss objectives, 3 seeds, 60,000+ series spanning RetailShiftBench and M5, with random-split controls---shows that regime-aware diagnosis separates optimization-type from bias-type failure, and that regime-aware training resolves the pooling-induced bias that capacity scaling cannot, for mean-type losses. A formal structural observation, that risk under evaluation-distribution contamination is affine in the pathology mixture weight, grounds these findings. Our work complements model ranking with mechanism-grounded, regime-oriented evaluation.

title: Super-Quadratic Quantum Speedups for Combinatorial Optimization via Tilted Walks
abstract: We introduce quantum tilted walks, a quantum algorithmic framework for solving exact combinatorial optimization problems. The framework applies an average of powers of a tilted Hamiltonian that biases the discriminant matrix of a base Markov chain (mixer) with the objective function. Our starting point is quantum short-path algorithms, which prepare the ground state of such a Hamiltonian and obtain super-quadratic speedups over exhaustive search for certain combinatorial optimization problems. Recently, Le Gall and Tamaki~(arXiv:2604.12131) developed a classical conditioning-and-search algorithm for weighted MAX-E$k$-LIN2 and weighted MAX-$k$-CSP. Under the same assumptions, their algorithm is only sub-quadratically slower than quantum short-path algorithms. Consequently, existing short-path algorithms do not establish a super-quadratic speedup over this stronger classical baseline. For maximization problems, we give conditions under which tilted walks increase the amplitude on the target state with high objective value when initialized from a starting state with lower objective value. This framework captures conditioning-and-search and yields super-quadratic speedups over it for the same problems. While our framework recovers quantum short-path algorithms as a special case, it neither requires ground-state preparation nor initialization in the ground state of the base mixer. We demonstrate these advantages on a synthetic optimization problem for which tilted walks achieve a super-quadratic speedup whereas the short-path algorithms do not.

title: Batik Motif Classification Using Textual Inversion in Low-Data Settings
abstract: Traditional batik motif classification faces significant challenges due to high intra-class variance and subtle interclass differences, particularly in low-data scenarios common in cultural heritage preservation. While convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformers have shown promise in general image classification, they struggle with domain-specific visual patterns when training data is limited. This study addresses the research gap by proposing a novel approach that integrates Textual Inversion with Vision-Language Models (VLMs) for robust classification of batik motifs under data constraints. We utilize a comprehensive dataset combining 600 manually labeled images from the Octadion corpus across three traditional motifs (Kawung, Parang, Mega Mendung) and 200 Nitik motif images from the Nitik-960 dataset, creating a unified four-class classification problem. Our experimental setup uses a few-shot learning paradigm, with only twenty exemplar images per motif for token learning, reserving the remaining samples for evaluation. The proposed method learns class-specific textual tokens through Textual Inversion, embedding them via a frozen CLIP text encoder while extracting visual features through CLIP’s visual encoder. A learnable projection layer with L2 regularization aligns text and image embeddings, enabling classification through cosine similarity. Compared with baseline methods, including Prototypical Networks, a CLIP linear probe, and attention-based few-shot approaches, our method achieves 77.1% classification accuracy on the combined dataset, a statistically significant 2.5% improvement over the strongest baseline (p < 0.05). Embedding visualizations reveal clear motif separation in the learned feature space, confirming the method’s ability to capture distinctive cultural patterns. Statistical significance testing across multiple random seeds confirms the robustness of our improvements. These findings demonstrate the potential of vision-language integration for cultural heritage classification tasks, opening new directions for preserving and digitizing traditional art forms through advanced AI techniques.

title: Exact spectral gaps for random Pauli rotations
abstract: We determine which representation sectors control the slowest convergence of random Pauli rotations and several local random quantum circuits. For $d=2^n$, the continuous Pauli walk has exact all-representation gaps $$\Delta_{\mathsf{SU}(d)}=\frac{d-8}{8(d-1)}\quad(n\ge4),\qquad \Delta_{\mathsf{PU}(d)}=\frac{d(d-3)}{8(d^2-1)}\quad(n\ge3).$$ The special-unitary gap is attained in $\bigwedge^8\mathbb{C}^d$ and is invisible to balanced moments, while the projective gap is already attained in a balanced fourth-moment representation. We obtain exact discrete and orthogonal Pauli analogues, exact finite-Clifford chain/path gaps, and dimension-independent all-representation Haar brickwork lower bounds; on three qubits every weighted Haar-$\mathsf{SU}(4)$ edge walk reduces to one universal principal-angle constant. For real complete-graph models, the entire ordinary fourth-tensor gap reduces to a quadratic-size occupation operator, is simple for every $n\ge4$, and has an expansion beginning $$\Delta_n^{(4)}=\frac{10}{9n}-\frac{88}{105n^2}+O(n^{-3}),$$ with competing branches separated only beyond all algebraic orders. For the two finite real Clifford complete-graph walks, this fourth-tensor mode is the exact all-representation group gap for every $n\ge144$; in the same range it simultaneously governs every ordinary even tensor degree $k\ge4$. Thus different representation scopes can have genuinely different slow modes.

title: Quantum Computing Frontiers: Volume-1
abstract: Quantum Computing Frontiers is a comprehensive academic and professional resource that presents a systematic exploration of quantum computing, quantum information, and emerging quantum technologies. The book begins with the foundations of classical computation and the physical motivation for quantum computing, progressing through quantum states, qubits, superposition, probability amplitudes, interference, measurement, and the mathematical foundations of quantum information. It provides detailed coverage of Hilbert spaces, linear operators, tensor products, density operators, unitary transformations, quantum mechanics postulates, Schrödinger dynamics, quantum noise, decoherence, and measurement processes. The text further examines qubit geometry, Bloch-sphere representation, multi-qubit systems, quantum measurements, state preparation, no-cloning, no-signaling, and quantum randomness, followed by an extensive treatment of quantum entanglement, Bell states, the EPR paradox, Bell and CHSH inequalities, quantum nonlocality, entanglement measures, and experimental perspectives. Applications of quantum technologies in computation, communication, cryptography, simulation, artificial intelligence, optimization, quantum error correction, distributed computing, quantum networks, quantum sensing, and metrology are also explored, providing readers with a broad understanding of current and emerging directions in the field. Designed for students, educators, researchers, engineers, and technology professionals, the book combines mathematical foundations, conceptual explanations, algorithms, illustrations, and practical perspectives to support learning, research, and innovation in quantum information science and next-generation computing technologies.

title: Tron-1B: Fast, Calibrated Typed Decisions with a Set-Attention Option Head
abstract: Applications built around large language models make many small decisions: which queue a ticket belongs to, whether a message is a prompt-injection attempt, how urgent a request is, whether an agent's step succeeded. Routing each of these through a generative LLM is slow, costly and hard to calibrate. We present Tron-1B, a 1.06-billion-parameter bidirectional encoder with a purpose-built decision head that answers typed questions (choose one option, rate on an ordered scale, or answer yes/no) about arbitrary text or JSON in a single forward pass, returning a calibrated probability for every option. The head pools each option's span, lets options attend to each other and to the question through a small permutation-equivariant set-attention option mixer, and scores them with a pairwise MLP; temperatures are fitted per question type and option count. A companion runtime, troncore, adds cross-request batching, an elimination tournament for more than 128 options, sliding windows for long inputs, and confidence-based abstention. evidence.title: Tron-1B: Fast, Calibrated Typed Decisions with a Set-Attention Option Head
evidence.abstract: Applications built around large language models make many small decisions: which queue a ticket belongs to, whether a message is a prompt-injection attempt, how urgent a request is, whether an agent's step succeeded. title: FREEBOARD: Permanently Restoring Security Margin in a Deployed Lattice-Based KEM
abstract: A module-lattice KEM standard fixes a small, discrete menu of parameter sets, each calibrated to a believed hardness level at the time of standardization. When an operator concludes, from their own analysis of implementation-level or systems-level attack optimizations that the standard's asymptotic cost model does not capture, that a deployed parameter set's effective margin has eroded below their risk tolerance, the smallest available lever is often a single-integer increase in module rank k, holding every other parameter, including the legacy compression parameters, fixed. This paper treats that decision as a first-class engineering question rather than an emergency patch. We present a reproducible methodology that combines a calibrated core-SVP margin estimate with an exact re-derivation of the decryption failure rate (DFR), and apply it to a case study: incrementing the module rank of a Category-5 module-lattice KEM parameter set (n=256, q=3329, k=4 to 5, eta1=eta2=2, compression parameters (du,dv)=(11,5) held fixed). Using a companion analysis's current estimate of the attack speedup, the deployed k=4 set sits within a bit of its NIST category floor (about 0.5 bits below it when two ring-symmetry credits are summed, about 3.7 bits above it counting one attack's credit), so the increment is chosen on a risk-tolerance judgment and not on a demonstrated deficit. The increment moves the effective margin by about 73 bits, a step roughly 140 times larger than the gap it closes, because no intermediate integer rank exists. Its permanent costs are +24.5% public-key size, +22.4% ciphertext size, up to +56% more field operations in the dominant matrix-vector step, and a DFR degradation from about 2^-177.1 to about 2^-142.6: a real, permanent worsening of correctness that runs counter to the intuition that more margin is uniformly better, and that must be checked explicitly rather than assumed. We argue that this class of change is structurally distinct from a stopgap: it has no scheduled replacement, it must be held to the same rigor as any official parameter set, and its costs are paid on every operation, forever. We call the resulting design point freeboard: a permanent, paid-for-once margin built in against a modeling gap, in the engineering sense the term is used for ship hulls and levees. We position it against from-scratch redesign with a different lever, joint re-optimization of the existing parameter tuple, and finer-grained algebraic structures, and give a permanent cost ledger and a decision checklist for operators. The margin figures are cost-model estimates, and the k=5 value is an extrapolation one rank beyond any published specification gate count.

title: El-Rakhawi Epistemic Resonance Architecture (ERA) A Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Hallucination-Free, Causally-Grounded Artificial Intelligence
abstract: The El-Rakhawi Epistemic Resonance Architecture (ERA) eliminates AI hallucination by transitioning models from statistical prediction to human-like, causally-grounded reasoning. ERA introduces a tripartite "System 2" cognitive framework: 1) A Neuro-Symbolic Causal World Model grounding facts in logical knowledge graphs, replacing mere statistical correlation; 2) The Epistemic Hesitation Protocol, mathematically quantifying uncertainty to empower AI to recognize knowledge boundaries and refuse unverified outputs; 3) An Internal Adversarial Verification Engine that actively attempts to falsify responses before release. Central to ERA is the El-Rakhawi Truth Certainty Equation, a mathematical metric ensuring every output meets a strict reliability threshold. This transforms AI into a reliable, ethically aligned cognitive partner. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23057666.

title: Beyond Transparency: How Meaningful Human Oversight Shapes Authenticity and Trust in Generative AI-Assisted Marketing
abstract: This dataset contains anonymized semi-structured interview data collected to explore Generation Z consumers' perceptions of Generative AI-assisted marketing content. The dataset focuses on AI disclosure, meaningful human oversight, perceived authenticity, and consumer trust. The interviews were conducted with six participants and were analyzed using a reflexive thematic analysis approach. The dataset is provided as supporting research data for the study entitled "Beyond Transparency: How Meaningful Human Oversight Shapes Authenticity and Trust in Generative AI-Assisted Marketing." Personally identifiable information has been removed or replaced to protect participant privacy.

title: Radiolaria OS: Computing, Assembled Around Intent
abstract: Radiolaria OS is an application execution kernel for organizing practical work around human intent. It brings together language models, programs, services and numerical tools while separating semantic proposals, bounded execution, evidence and decisions by local resource owners. Its purpose is to support applications that can respond to changing requirements and resources without giving an individual model unrestricted control over the activity. The reference materials illustrate complementary aspects of this architecture. Football demonstrates exchange of computed material between independent owners and a separately authorized mock booking. Wedding connects model-returned changes to computation and follows recorded quantum results through validation and consumption. An ephemeral workspace demonstrates selective continuation after a resource disappears. Additional materials describe time, memory, provenance, experience-based allocation and independently examined model-authored extensions. This record archives the eight assets of the GitHub release radiolaria-os-reference-g6b6f-v01, first published on 29 September 2026. It includes a whitepaper, an editable presentation and its PDF, a Geometry Atlas, an explanatory XML Reader, a historical reader-evaluation bundle, and the complete declared public source export in XML and ZIP formats. The explanatory Reader is intended for architectural understanding; the large source export is intended for indexed or tool-assisted inspection, not a single model prompt. Akhtanin Andrii led the architecture and research. AI tools, including ChatGPT/Codex and Gemini, assisted implementation, analysis, documentation, translation and visual preparation. Recorded model interactions are identified as experimental material, not human peer review. The human author remains responsible for the work. The documentation distinguishes controlled examples, historical provider responses, mock effects, retained evidence and untested deployment assumptions. Licensing is component-specific. Code is licensed under AGPL-3.0-only. New explanatory author text and original diagrams are licensed under CC BY 4.0. Verbatim code excerpts, historical material, third-party content and embedded font subsets retain their applicable notices. These are not alternative blanket licenses for the entire deposit. See RIGHTS.md and the license notices in the source bundle.

title: Discrete algebraic channel modeling and information-theoretic security bounds for quantum key distribution protocols
authors: V. S. J. R. K. Padminivalli
Poranki V. L. R. N. Sudha
abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) provides information-theoretically secure key exchange whose security is guaranteed by the laws of quantum mechanics.This paper presents a rigorous discrete algebraic channel model for QKD transmission, representing the noisy quantum channel as a stochastic operator over the finite field GF(2^n) and deriving tight information-theoretic security bounds using Renyi entropy formulations over discrete probability spaces.The proposed framework extends the BB84 and E91 protocols by incorporating a novel algebraic error reconciliation algorithm based on low-density paritycheck (LDPC) codes over GF(28) that reduces information leakage during post-processing by @

title: G-XCI: A Conditional Multi-View Audit of Stability and Cross-View Rank Agreement in Tabular Feature Attributions
abstract: Post hoc feature attributions are often interpreted from a single run, although their reproducibility and agreement with other explanatory views can depend on resampling, model family, representation, audit lens, output orientation, and inspection scope. We evaluate G-XCI as a conditional three-readout audit protocol. LAS measures reproducibility of an aggregate ranking derived from held-out Monte-Carlo Shapley attributions; GRS summarizes cross-seed variance of a specified global score profile; SCC measures Kendall tau-b agreement between the aggregate attribution ranking and a chosen global ranking. Across three tabular datasets, three model families, five stratified repeats, four global audit lenses, three inspection scopes, GRA ablations, and representation variants, Adult Income changed SCC sign with K, while audit-lens and representation changes materially altered SCC. Targeted supplementary audits showed that complementing the WDBC binary output reversed the mean GRA-based SCC sign in all nine model-scale combinations while leaving absolute local Shapley rankings unchanged, whereas forcing Standard GRA, absolute Spearman-to-output, and output permutation onto the same 128 held-out cases preserved all 27 original mean-SCC signs. A short lemma shows that robust-z followed by min-max equals direct min-max for nonconstant sequences. In the tested tabular binary-classification settings, G-XCI supports conditional auditing of aggregate-ranking reproducibility and cross-view rank agreement under a declared audit contract; it does not establish universal explanation correctness.

title: ODRF: An R Package for Oblique Decision Tree and Its Random Forest
abstract: The classification and regression tree (CART) and Random Forest (RF) are popular machine learning methods that involve selecting one predictor at a time as the splitting variable for each node.The use of linear combinations of predictors as splitting variables is one of the popular extensions of CART and RF, known as Oblique Decision Trees (ODT), and hence ODT-based Random Forests (ODRF).Recent studies have also shown the theoretical advantages of ODT and ODRF over CART and RF.However, there is still no integrated and efficient software package that can demonstrate the numerical advantages of ODT and ODRF.To fill this gap, we make several modifications to the existing algorithms and develop an R package ODRF for both ODT() and ODRF().In addition, the R package includes a series of new functions, such as ODT-based boosting trees (BODT), the ensemble version of BODT (ODBT), ODT visualization (plot.ODT), and an online update function for ODT (online.ODT).The main part of ODRF is executed using the Rcpp package.This paper presents the basic idea of our modifications and illustrates the use of the package.Through numerical experiments, ODRF was compared with other packages of decision trees and forests, showing a clear overall improvement in classification and regression tasks.

title: Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) Untuk Klasifikasi Konektivitas Bandara
abstract: Jaringan penerbangan global merupakan sistem transportasi kompleks yang secara alamiah membentuk struktur graf keruangan (spasial). Pemahaman terhadap hierarki konektivitas bandara sangat krusial bagi analisis rute dan optimalisasi infrastruktur. Namun, pemodelan data relasional berstruktur graf memiliki tantangan tersendiri jika diselesaikan menggunakan pendekatan machine learning konvensional berskala tabular. Penelitian ini mengusulkan penerapan arsitektur Deep Learning berbasis graf, yaitu Graph Convolutional Network (GCN), untuk mengklasifikasikan tingkat konektivitas bandara di seluruh dunia. Dataset yang digunakan merupakan rekaman operasional penerbangan global tahun 2024 yang .merepresentasikan 7.698 simpul (bandara) dan 36.589 sisi (edge) unik antarbandara, yang dibentuk dari 66.316 baris data rute mentah (satu baris per maskapai per rute) setelah melalui tahap pembersihan data.. Karena dataset tidak memiliki anotasi kelas yang eksplisit, algoritma Fuzzy C-Means (FCM) diterapkan secara unsupervised berdasarkan metrik degree centrality untuk menghasilkan pseudo-ground truth. Melalui metode ini, bandara diklasifikasikan ke dalam tiga kategori: Rendah, Sedang, dan Tinggi. Arsitektur GCN dirancang menggunakan dua lapisan konvolusi graf dengan fungsi aktivasi ReLU, teknik regularisasi Dropout dengan rasio 0.5, serta fungsi keluaran klasifikasi Softmax. Pembagian data dilakukan menggunakan skema transductive node masking dengan rasio 70% data latih, 15% data validasi, dan 15% data uji guna menjaga keutuhan topologi jaringan. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan bahwa model GCN yang dioptimasi menggunakan algoritma Adam pada 900 Epoch mampu memprediksi kelas konektivitas dengan tingkat akurasi keseluruhan sebesar 95% dan Macro F1-Score sebesar 79%. Secara keseluruhan, penelitian ini membuktikan bahwa algoritma GCN efektif dan tangguh dalam menangkap dan mengagregasi fitur atribut spasial secara simultan dengan topologi koneksi untuk pemodelan node classification pada sistem transportasi udara skala besar yang tidak seimbang (imbalanced data).

title: Benchmarking Generative Models for Near-Surface Data Assimilation on Real Station Observations
abstract: Weather reanalysis products rely on computationally intensive numerical weather predictions followed by data assimilation that corrects the forecast toward observations. Recent advances in deep generative models offer a cheaper alternative that shifts much of this cost from inference to offline training. However, existing generative approaches have been evaluated on synthetic observations or under different datasets and evaluation schemes, making it unclear which design choices improve real-world data assimilation. We present the first controlled benchmark of generative data assimilation for single-time near-surface analysis from real weather station observations. Using 11,849 NOAA MADIS stations across the contiguous United States and four near-surface variables, we hold the dataset, observation operator, and deep learning architecture fixed, and measure spatial generalization at held-out stations. The benchmark compares the major design choices proposed for generative data assimilation, including diffusion versus flow matching, pixel versus latent-space formulations, and multiple inference-time conditioning strategies, against a classical 3D-Var baseline. The benchmark reveals three conclusions. First, the best generative methods outperform 3D-Var (35.7% vs. 33.3% RMSE improvement over ERA5), although 3D-Var receives the ERA5 field at the analysis time as its background and the generative methods receive none. Second, full-gradient guidance consistently outperforms stop-gradient and initial-noise optimization. Third, other choices provide little measurable benefit: diffusion and flow matching perform nearly identically under matched conditions, and latent-space variable mixing does not help. Both advantages widen when stations are sparse. Together, these results identify which components of generative data assimilation improve spatial generalization in near-surface analysis.

title: Exact Maximum Likelihood Decoding beyond Treewidth via Rank-Decomposition Dynamic Programming
abstract: Maximum-likelihood decoding provides an optimal decoding strategy for quantum error correction under stochastic Pauli noise. However, computing logical-class probabilities is challenging, and the leading exact tensor-network contraction requires time exponential in treewidth. In this work, we introduce a new decoding algorithm based on rank-decomposition dynamic programming (Rank DP). We express decoding partition functions with independent local fault factors as quadratic sums of powers and apply Rank DP. The resulting exact evaluator has arithmetic complexity polynomial in the input size and exponential in the Tanner graph's rank-width with respect to the fault partition, including decomposition construction. After Gaussian elimination, it gives polynomial-time decoding for punctured quantum Reed-Muller codes and a Steane-concatenated family with growing distance under independent single-qubit Pauli noise. Standard contraction of the corresponding tensor networks requires superpolynomial time. A nonnegative realization gives relative floating-point error bounds under explicit arithmetic assumptions. Numerical experiments demonstrate runtime advantages over the tested tensor-network implementations on selected code-capacity and circuit-level instances, with full likelihood evaluation for Reed-Muller codes up to $1{,}023$ qubits. We further use these likelihoods to learn circuit noise parameters from syndromes, evaluate rare postselection probabilities, and quantify decoder optimality gaps. Our work opens new avenues for exploiting algebraic structure in quantum decoding and noise characterization.

title: When, Not How Much: Evaluating Time-Series Foundation Models on Sparse Events
abstract: Pretrained time-series foundation models (TSFMs) are evaluated as forecasters of future values, yet for sparse series many decisions depend only on which future periods contain activity. Standard benchmarks do not assess this. On five sparse datasets, we rank positions within forecast windows that contain both events and zeros. The released point forecasts of 12 TSFMs improve chance-corrected average precision over training-free references by at most 0.031, and in chance-corrected AUC the median TSFM falls below them on every dataset. With event supervision, linear probes of six frozen backbones improve on their backbone's point forecast in 29 of 30 backbone--dataset pairs. Averaging the predicted quantiles instead of taking their median improves the ranking of most TSFMs that forecast the median, and on two datasets the strongest such outputs rival the probes. The probes' advantage over raw-context learners depends on the dataset, and under the same probe, pretrained features outperform randomly initialized ones for five of six backbones. For sparse-event ranking, released point forecasts thus add little over simple references, whereas lightweight event heads on frozen TSFMs rank events better than these forecasts, and the best of them exceed gradient-boosted trees trained on the raw context on three of the five datasets. More broadly, assessing pretrained forecasters on tasks beyond value forecasting requires reporting their outputs, supervised probes of their representations, and raw-context and randomized controls side by side, since each supports a different conclusion.

title: Frame Differential On-Policy Self-Distillation for Video Reasoning
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has substantially improved the reasoning ability of multimodal language models through verifiable rewards and increasingly fine-grainedvisual or temporal credit assignment. In video reasoning, however, current RL methods typically train with a fixed sparse frame budget: increasing the number of frames makes autoregressive rollouts expensive, while too few frames may miss temporally localized events and fine-grained visual details. We present \textbf{Frame Differential On-Policy Self-Distillation (FD-OPSD)}, which transfers the useful evidence of dense frame observations to a sparse frame policy during RL training. FD-OPSD compares the policy's token level preferences for the same sampled response under sparse and dense views, and distills the resulting frame differential signal without an external teacher or dense autoregressive rollout. The method preserves sparse-frame rollouts and leaves inference unchanged. Across Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Qwen3-VL-4B on six video reasoning benchmarks, FD-OPSD yields higher overall average performance than the strongest corresponding GRPO, T-GRPO, or Video-KTR baselines across the 16, 32, and 64 frame evaluation settings. These results show that dense visual evidence can be transferred selectively during training through token level self-distillation while retaining sparse frame rollouts and unchanged inference.

title: Classify and Label the Content from the Cross-Cultural Misogynistic Meme Detection Using Zero-shot Prompts
abstract: Online misogyny increasingly appears in multimodal formats such as memes. Memes combine text and images to convey humor, sarcasm, and ideology. Misogynistic meaning is often implicit and culturally grounded. A meme interpreted as harmful in one cultural setting may be perceived differently in another. Based on the complex scenario of cross-cultural misogynistic meme detection, we proposed to conduct predictions using large language models (LLMs) through zero-shot prompts in the absenceof training datasets. This enables our method to effectively address the key pain points such as the difficulty in annotating the training dataset, the high cost and long time consumption of manually labeling the training dataset labels. We applied this zero-shot prompts method to the Tamil (India) MDMD dataset. The best model results achieved Macro F1-score and Accuracy of 0.628995 and 0.696629 respectively for Task A: Single-culture prediction. Overall contexts including Indian context, Chinesecontext, and Western context, the best model results achieved Macro F1-score and Accuracy of 0.601143 and 0.695693 respectively for Task B: Cross-cultural prediction. This approach of deliberately not using the training dataset for fine-tuning and training large language models (LLMs) or pre-trained models enables our method to have greater flexibility in real-world scenarios. For furtherinformation, the project code and user’s guide is available from https://github.com/WangKongQiang/CC-MMD_Grand_Challenge_ICMI_2026.

title: A Comparative Study on Transformer-Based Deep Learning Model for Network Traffic Classification
abstract: Network Traffic Classification (NTC) represents a fundamental pillar of modern cybersecurity, especially as encrypted traffic now exceeds 70% of global internet volume. Conventional methods like deep packet inspection (DPI) experience severe performance degradation in these environments, necessitating adaptive sequence models. This study presents an empirical comparison of four deep learning architectures: Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), and Transformers. We validated the models using a real-world telemetry dataset from Jabatan Data Negara (JDN), Malaysia. This repository spans 12,000 encrypted traffic flows across 648 unique application classes. To ensure strict experimental reproducibility, we partitioned the dataset using a balanced, stratified sampling configuration. The compiled corpus included 5,600 jitter profiles and 5,400 bandwidth measurements to support a comprehensive, future-driven behavioral evaluation. Experimental results demonstrate that the Transformer model achieves an optimal balance between computational throughput and classification precision. The proposed architecture achieved 99.60% accuracy while maintaining a wire-speed core throughput of 12.4 Gbps. Consequently, the 1D Convolutional Neural Network exhibits poor optimization stability for temporal sequences, yielding an accuracy of only 65.13%. This empirical work demonstrates that while Transformers are ideal for centralized backbone monitoring, an ultra-lightweight RNN with only 2,803 parameters offers a highly resource-aware alternative for edge deployment.

title: AI-Enabled Student Relationship Management: A Conceptual Framework for Digital Transformation in Higher Education
abstract: This paper develops a conceptual framework of AI-enabled Student Relationship Management (SRM) as a driver of digital transformation in higher education. Grounded on relationship marketing theory, the framework integrates the Nordic School perspective of value co-creation with the Industrial Marketing and Purchasing (IMP) network approach and extends the traditional Customer Relationship Management (CRM) framework to higher education. The proposed model conceptualises students as both customers and partners and positions artificial intelligence (AI) as an integrative layer connecting the strategic, operational, and analytical dimensions of SRM. The framework suggests that AI enhances predictive decision-making, personalised engagement, and adaptive relationship management, transforming SRM into a data-driven ecosystem. The study contributes an integrated theoretical perspective linking AI, SRM, and digital transformation and provides a foundation for future empirical research.

title: Interview Dataset: Beyond Transparency: How Meaningful Human Oversight Shapes Authenticity and Trust in Generative AI-Assisted Marketing
abstract: This dataset contains anonymized semi-structured interview data collected to explore Generation Z consumers' perceptions of Generative AI-assisted marketing content. The dataset focuses on AI disclosure, meaningful human oversight, perceived authenticity, and consumer trust. The interviews were conducted with six participants and were analyzed using a reflexive thematic analysis approach. The dataset is provided as supporting research data for the study entitled "Beyond Transparency: How Meaningful Human Oversight Shapes Authenticity and Trust in Generative AI-Assisted Marketing." Personally identifiable information has been removed or replaced to protect participant privacy.

title: LASO-Σ Machine: Adaptive Predictive Memory, Governance, and Recovery Architecture
abstract: LASO-Σ — One-Page Summary Adaptive Predictive Memory Machine LASO-Σ proposes a machine architecture in which memory is treated not as passive storage, but as an adaptive predictive state. The system does not only retrieve historical information. It evaluates whether that information improves future prediction, estimates confidence and contamination risk, regulates persistence, and measures recovery when the environment changes. The central architectural transformation is: Memory as stored information→Memory as governed predictive state\boxed{ \text{Memory as stored information} \rightarrow \text{Memory as governed predictive state} } The complete machine is represented as: LASO-Σ=Fθ+Mt+Ut+Ct+Gt+Rt\boxed{ LASO\text{-}\Sigma = F_\theta+M_t+U_t+C_t+G_t+R_t } where FθF_\theta is the predictor, MtM_t adaptive memory, UtU_t usefulness measurement, CtC_t contamination assessment, GtG_t governance, and RtR_t recovery. What the reconstructed experiments show Experiment 36 demonstrated that historical information has conditional rather than universal predictive value. Under random dynamics, real history produced approximately the same performance as erased history: 50.04%vs.50.03%.50.04\%\quad\text{vs.}\quad50.03\%. Under increasingly structured environments, the historical advantage increased: Environment Real history Erased history Difference Random 50.04% 50.03% +0.01 pp Markov 52.73% 50.18% +2.55 pp Motif 62.13% 50.00% +12.13 pp Periodic 69.76% 50.00% +19.76 pp This supports the hypothesis that useful memory should depend on the predictive structure of the environment. Experiment 40 demonstrated the complementary governance problem. In the reconstructed 100-seed test, governance reduced end-of-attack memory distortion from 1.000 to 0.302, a reduction of 69.8 percentage points, while clean pre-attack accuracy remained 92.27% in both systems. However, governed adaptation was slower immediately after the attack. This demonstrates why LASO-Σ must optimize both protection and continued learning rather than simply suppressing memory updates. The LASO-Σ filter The machine evaluates memory through: Persistence, Retrieval, Usefulness, Temporal Structure, Adaptive Persistence, Contamination, Governance, Recovery, Energy, Future Memory Value\boxed{ Persistence,\; Retrieval,\; Usefulness,\; Temporal\ Structure,\; Adaptive\ Persistence,\; Contamination,\; Governance,\; Recovery,\; Energy,\; Future\ Memory\ Value } This provides a broader benchmark than retrieval accuracy alone. Industry relevance The architecture is applicable wherever previously useful information can become harmful after environmental change: robotics, autonomous systems, manufacturing, energy systems, cybersecurity, supply chains, agriculture, industrial control and long-running AI agents. The important research question is therefore not simply: “Can an AI remember?”\text{“Can an AI remember?”} but: “Which memories should remain influential under the current and future environment?”\boxed{ \text{“Which memories should remain influential under the current and future environment?”} } What has not yet been established LASO-Σ has not yet been demonstrated to outperform every existing commercial AI-memory or retrieval architecture. Such a conclusion requires controlled benchmarking under identical data, compute, latency and hardware conditions. The decisive benchmark must measure: Accuracy, Memory Gain, Contamination, Recovery, Governance Loss, Latency, Energy, Future Memory Usefulness\boxed{ Accuracy,\; Memory\ Gain,\; Contamination,\; Recovery,\; Governance\ Loss,\; Latency,\; Energy,\; Future\ Memory\ Usefulness } Therefore the present results establish a testable architectural hypothesis, not a universal superiority claim. Proceed The next stage is to implement the complete LASO-Σ machine as one frozen executable architecture and conduct controlled baseline comparisons. Proceed to full LASO-Σ implementation and industrial benchmarking.\boxed{ \textbf{Proceed to full LASO-Σ implementation and industrial benchmarking.} } The decisive test is: Can LASO-Σ remember selectively, predict better, resist contamination, recover rapidly, and operate at acceptable energy cost?\boxed{ \text{Can LASO-Σ remember selectively, predict better, resist contamination, recover rapidly, and operate at acceptable energy cost?} } If future controlled experiments demonstrate these properties simultaneously, the evidence would support a broader transition from persistent information retrieval toward governed predictive memory. LASO-Σ: persistent intelligence without persistent error.\boxed{ \textbf{LASO-Σ: persistent intelligence without persistent error.} } LASO-Σ Machine: Adaptive Predictive Memory, Governance, and Recovery Architecture Authors: Egidijus Kasiulevičius, Aušra Kasiulevičienė, Ąžuolas Kasiulevičius, Saulė KasiulevičiūtėDOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23052825License: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 — Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International

title: Comparative Study of Acoustic Features for Spoken Digit Recognition in Algerian Arabic Dialects and Accented French
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study of six acoustic feature representations for spoken digit recognition in Algerian Arabic dialects and accented French. The evaluated features include MFCC, MFCC with temporal derivatives, Log-Mel filterbank, LFCC, GFCC, and PNCC. Experiments are conducted on a corpus of isolated digits (0--99) collected from four Algerian regions (Algiers, Blida, Tizi-Ouzou, Sétif), covering both native dialectal speech and French-accented variants. Three classifiers---SVM, CNN, and BiLSTM---are compared to assess feature--model interactions. Results demonstrate that MFCC provides strong baselines across all regions, while GFCC achieves the highest accuracy (up to 94.4%) for dialectal speech. BiLSTM exhibits training instability with conventional features but improves significantly with perceptually motivated representations. These findings provide the first systematic benchmark for 100-class Algerian Arabic digit recognition and highlight the importance of feature selection in low-resource speech processing.

title: Cryptographic framework for secure data transmission in IoT networks using lightweight hybrid encryption
abstract: As the Internet of Things (IoT) continues to grow at an exponential rate, securing the transmission of data among various types of heterogeneous resources with limited capacity has become more challenging than ever before.To address this challenge, we propose a lightweight cryptographic framework that integrates optimized symmetric and asymmetric encryption algorithms and secure communication protocols, which can significantly enhance the security of IoT communications.Specifically, we describe an architecture for our new cryptographic framework that utilizes AES-128 and ECC-based key exchanges combined with dynamic tokenization and hashing for integrity verification -to provide confidentiality, authentication, and integrity of the communicated data.In addition, our experimental results show that more than double (37%) the cryptographic throughput compared to other traditional methods; over 22% less memory overhead than traditional methods; and 19% less energy consumed to process the same amount of data as traditional methods.Furthermore, the system reduces the potential for man-in-the-middle and spoofing attacks by 46% when using secure MQTT or HTTPS basis of transmission layers within the overall architecture.

title: Reconstruction-Aided Short-Term Power Forecasting for Data-Limited Distributed PV Stations
abstract: Short-term forecasting is difficult at distributed photovoltaic (PV) stations that retain hourly energy records but lack power measurements at fine time intervals and site-specific irradiance. We propose a reconstruction-aided method for one-step-ahead forecasting under these conditions. Variational mode decomposition (VMD) separates the target-station energy sequence and the reference-station energy and power sequences into multiscale modes. Hilbert modal features and a multidimensional similarity score identify suitable reference modes, and extremely randomized trees (ExtraTrees) reconstruct the target station's 5-min power profile while preserving each recorded hourly energy total. For the irradiance input, the clear-sky index reduces periodic effects, VMD captures multiscale disturbances at observed grid cells, and ExtraTrees completes global horizontal irradiance (GHI) at the unobserved target cell. Reconstructed power, completed GHI, periodic time features, and aggregated neighboring-station power are then supplied to LightGBM to predict target power at the next time step. Tests use 2021 measurements from distributed PV stations in a UK region and CAMS irradiance on a 7 × 7 grid. The normalized mean absolute error was 0.377%, the normalized root mean square error was 1.168%, and the coefficient of determination was 0.990. The results indicate that the method can recover fine-resolution power and local irradiance from limited target-station information and improve short-term forecasts for data-limited distributed PV stations.

evidence.title: Reconstruction-Aided Short-Term Power Forecasting for Data-Limited Distributed PV Stations
evidence.abstract: Short-term forecasting is difficult at distributed photovoltaic (PV) stations that retain hourly energy records but lack power measurements at fine time intervals and site-specific irradiance. We propose a reconstruction-aided method for one-step-ahead forecasting under these conditions. Variational mode decomposition (VMD) separates the target-station energy sequence and the reference-station energy and power sequences into multiscale modes. Hilbert modal features and a multidimensional similarity score identify suitable reference modes, and extremely randomized trees (ExtraTrees) reconstruct the target station's 5-min power profile while preserving each recorded hourly energy total. For the irradiance input, the clear-sky index reduces periodic effects, VMD captures multiscale disturbances at observed grid cells, and ExtraTrees completes global horizontal irradiance (GHI) at the unobserved target cell. Reconstructed power, completed GHI, periodic time features, and aggregated neighboring-station power are then supplied to LightGBM to predict target power at the next time step. Tests use 2021 measurements from distributed PV stations in a UK region and CAMS irradiance on a 7 × 7 grid. The normalized mean absolute error was 0.377%, the normalized root mean square error was 1.168%, and the coefficient of determination was 0.990. The results indicate that the method can recover fine-resolution power and local irradiance from limited target-station information and improve short-term forecasts for data-limited distributed PV stations.

title: When Should AI Intervene? : Effects of AI Agents’ Help Type and Intervention Timing on Acceptance Intention and Overall Satisfaction
abstract: 최근 AI의 발전으로 사용자의 요청에 반응하던 반응형 에이전트는 사용자의 맥락을 해석해 먼저 개입하는 능동형 에이전트로 진화하고 있다. 이는 단순한 도구를 넘어 상황을 이해하고 스스로 판단·결정하는 방식으로 확장되고 있다. 그러나 이러한 선제적 도움방식이 사용자의 자율성과 유능감에 어떤 심리적 비용을 초래하고, 궁극적으로 도움 수용과 지불 의향, 시스템 만족도에 어떤 영향을 미치는지는 아직 충분히 밝혀지지 않았다. 이에 본 연구는 AI에이전트의 도움방식(반응적 vs. 선제적)과 개입 시점(전·중·후)이 사용자 심리적 경험에 미치는 영향을 실증적으로 규명하는 것을 목적으로 한다. 장보기 상황의 스마트카트 시나리오를 활용한 2×3 집단 간 설계 설문조사를 실시하였으며, 구조모형 분석 및 질적 분석을 통해 가설을 검증하였다. 분석 결과, 선제적 도움은 반응적 도움에 비해 자율성·유능감 상실을 모두 유의하게 높였으며, 자율성 상실은 도움 수용 의향과 지불 의향 모두를 저하시키는 것으로 나타났다. 주목할 만한 점은 유능감 상실이 도움 수용 의향은 낮추면서도 지불 의향은 오히려 높이는 패턴을 보였다는 것으로, 이는 능력에 대한 불안을 느끼는 사용자일수록 AI의 도움을 적극적으로 수용하기보다, 실수를 예방하기 위한 안전장치로 인식하여 비용 지불을 정당화하는 경향이 있음을 시사한다. 또한 시스템 만족도에는 지불 의향보다 도움 수용 의향이 더 큰 영향을 미치는 것으로 나타나, AI 도움에 대한 심리적 수용이 만족도를 결정하는 핵심 요인임이 확인되었다. 본 연구는 AI 에이전트 설계 시 기능의 정확도보다 사용자의 자율성과 유능감을 지지하는 방식으로 도움방식과 개입 시점을 설계해야 함을 제안한다.
